text: Goll mac Morna was a one-eyed warrior of the Irish Fianna. His story ties back to the place called Keshcorran. Fionn once gave Goll a daughter in marriage to reward him. Yet the two leaders were not always friends. Once Fionn found Goll sleeping by the river Shannon and let the tired one-eyed warrior rest. Still the old hatred did not die. After he was freed, Fionn killed the grandson Fer I, and the bloodshed began again. At last Goll was pushed to the far edge of Ireland. There he passed many days without food or drink and grew wild with want. A low-ranked Fianna man, Mac Smaile, struck him down. The quarrel did not end with his death. The feud sputtered on until the Fianna fell at Gabhair. Some tales send Goll to a new home on the magic islands of the west. His story is often confused with that of Balor. Balor was a Fomorian king with one evil eye that killed by a glance. Goll also meets Lugh, the hero who killed his own grandfather Balor. Goll may be the same as the one-eyed salmon of Assaroe, a being also named Goll Essa Rua. In another tale an Ulster champion strikes down a rival hero named Goll mac Carbada, in a matching contest.
